goal: Sort the small objects on the table by category into the three baskets: all objects of one category go into one basket, and the three categories go into the three different baskets. Then put the arm back home.
instruction_templates: Sort the objects by category into the three baskets.
success: A label is 'in' a basket when the object's root origin xy lies inside the basket's bbox footprint (convex hull of the oriented 3D bbox projected to xy) and its root z is strictly above the bbox's lowest z. For each of basket0, basket1, basket2: at least one of the three categories (cat0, cat1, cat2, each category = all its object instances) must have ALL of its objects inside that basket. Because a basket needs a whole category and each category can only be in one basket, this forces a bijection: every category fully in its own distinct basket, so every object ends up in a basket. Which category goes into which basket is free (any permutation is accepted).

Settled: for each i in 0..2, every object of category cat_i has root z - (top z of the world-frame bbox of basket_i) < 0.01 m. NOTE the pairing cat_i with basket_i is hard-coded here regardless of which basket the category is actually in; because objects resting on the table or inside baskets are normally below the basket rim, this only fails if an object is lifted (e.g. held in the gripper) higher than 0.01 m above basket top.
All target robots back at start end-effector pose: |dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m and rotation <= 20 degrees (all_robot_back_to_origin defaults).
evaluation: Checked after every action (the reward manager step runs after each action's control sequence completes). One stage: all of the above must hold at the same step, with the arm home; success at the first such step (all objects released, since objects held in the gripper would typically be above the 0.01 m rim threshold). Otherwise fails at step_lim=1100 actions. Process score (partial only): transition mode scores 15, 40, 100 for 1, 2, 3 baskets correctly filled with grippers open (open fraction >= 0.8).
objects: basket0: basket (category basket, index 2), fixed, x=-0.28, y=0.05, no rotation (leftmost, lowest x)
basket1: basket (category basket, index 3), fixed, x=0.0, y=0.05 (middle)
basket2: basket (category basket, index 4), fixed, x=+0.28, y=0.05 (rightmost, highest x)

cat0, cat1, cat2 (label prefixes; objects are labelled cat0_*, cat1_*, cat2_* by category): 3 distinct categories drawn at random from {toy_car (index 0-4), action_camera, pen (index 0,1,4), watch (index 0-2), garage (index 14,15)}; each category gets 1 to 3 instances (select_instance_nums [1,3], interpreted as an inclusive range, duplicates of the same model allowed). Scattered on the table: x in [-0.43,0.43], y in [-0.23,0.0], random yaw within +/-60 deg, 0.01 m margin.
needs_memory_or_language: none (the instruction is fixed; the agent must visually group objects by category and the baskets can take any category).
end_requirements: All target arms back within 0.15 m per axis and 20 degrees of start end-effector pose at the moment of success.
notes: Count of objects varies (3 to 9 total). The check does not require uniformly-sorted-to-specific baskets; any bijection of categories to baskets is accepted. Object membership uses the object's root origin xy-inside-basket-footprint test, so an object leaning over the rim is judged by its origin. Baskets are fixed (geometry, not movable by design). Details of the asset origin are not determinable statically.
